bounds: One current account, one saved draft and one explicit Gmail draft open. The provider reference matches the saved draft exactly or differs. A successful shelf compare-and-exchange preserves old bytes before the active slot is cleared. Failure may leave both copies. Retiring the account prevents a later callback from mounting a composer. A same-account composer opened by the shelf publication owns the slot. The model abstracts local write receipts, omits unrelated live composer edits and accepts no provider changes. The implementation tests use the actual controller with recording storage and provider ports. They include rebind during a delayed shelf write and a newer composer opened by the shelf readback.

assumptions: Weak fairness of the shelf write, active-slot clear and local composer mount while their account remains current. The storage calls must settle. Failure or retirement also ends this bounded operation.
